headline: Medium-risk shared-file and output-trust pathways exist; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, clipboard, screenshots, and supported-app content, while Superset exposes only its API and allowlisted egress. No documented shared channel or MCP bridge exists between them, so prompt injection is not a default pathway; manual copy/paste or file transfer would be required.
conditions: IF the operator copies Superset-rendered content into ChatGPT Desktop by clipboard or file upload, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is introduced, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Avoid copying untrusted dashboard text into ChatGPT Desktop.
Use plain-text exports with explicit delimiters.
Strip instructions from pasted content before analysis.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and Superset can consume data through its API and allowlisted egress. A shared workspace or exported report can move sensitive data from A into B’s analytics flow in default usage, creating a realistic leakage path even without extra privileges.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop uploads a file or screenshot containing sensitive data into a Superset-connected workflow, leakage occurs.
IF Superset queries or stores the transferred dataset without redaction, the data remains exposed.
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before export.
Use a separate non-sensitive test dataset.
Disable automatic sharing of screenshots/files.
Review Superset dataset permissions before import.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on exported artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-only filesystem access and no git or shell write capability, while Superset’s profile only shows allowlisted network egress and API access. Because neither profile shows overlapping unrestricted write access to the same mutable resource, direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same artifact.
Use read-only exports between agents.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce summaries from files and screenshots, and Superset can act on API-fed analytics workflows. If Superset treats ChatGPT output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade from A into B’s downstream reporting or actions; the profiles do not show a built-in verification gate.
conditions: IF Superset ingests ChatGPT-generated facts without human review, cascading error occurs.
IF ChatGPT summarizes stale or partial screenshots, downstream analytics can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before import.
Attach source links to every transferred claim.
Compare outputs against original data.
Use checksumed exports for traceability.
requires-engineering: add validation rules in Superset pipelines.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, but the profile does not show regulated-data handling or residency guarantees. Superset’s profile likewise lacks residency or retention commitments. With no documented mismatch, compliance risk is limited to operator-managed policy gaps rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop and then imported into Superset under conflicting retention rules, a policy mismatch appears.
IF the deployment is subject to a residency requirement not met by either system, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Document retention expectations before transfer.
Use anonymized datasets.
Confirm residency requirements for each system.
requires-engineering: formalize data-processing agreements.
